title: Mask Atelier
premise: A master-apprentice relay in an old opera house papier-mache workshop. Lu Qing and A-Tang guard the white-faced Cao Cao headdress; A-Tang and A-Lin look nearly identical except for hair ornaments; after the vermilion lacquer prop chest burns it must be avoided; oil-stained pattern book, count memory, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_master: A mask craftsman around forty, indigo short jacket dusted with pigment powder, right hand often gripping a wolf-hair brush, brows deeply furrowed.
states.lacquer_burn_arm: The same Lu Qing: right arm wrapped in white cloth burned by raw lacquer, brush switched to the left hand, jacket cuff charred black.
states.eyes_closed_dead: Lu Qing has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the workshop wooden couch, indigo short jacket covering his chest.

states.young_apprentice: A fifteen-year-old apprentice girl with twin topknots, a vermilion bib apron, vermilion paint on her fingertips, keen eyes.
states.adult_master: A woman master in her early twenties, still wearing the vermilion apron, hair in a neat bun, steady gaze.

states.intact: A freshly papier-mached white-faced Cao Cao headdress, silk beard black and neat, gold leaf on the crest still unworn.
states.lacquer_cracked: The same white-faced Cao Cao headdress: white face cracked open to hemp cloth core, beard tangled, gold leaf peeling.
states.rebacked: The white-faced Cao Cao headdress after rebacking: white face smooth, beard re-combed, gold leaf patched but slightly paler.

states.intact: A thread-bound face-pattern model book, vermilion and ink sketching painted-face formulas on xuan paper, cover stamped with a 'Lu's' vermilion seal.

states.intact: A large vermilion lacquer prop chest, twin-dragon relief on the lid, copper lock gleaming, blue cloth lining.

states.disguised_anew: A-Lin after a makeover still wears the peacock plume askew; a greasepaint scar on the temple, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk, mask craftsman Lu Qing pushes open the papier-mache atelier wooden door, both hands cradling the freshly papier-mached white-faced Cao Cao headdress.
A row of five tung-oil lamps hangs under the papier-mache atelier beam; Lu Qing wipes soot from each with a cloth.
Two pairs of copper clappers hang by the door; Lu Qing brushes them and they ring clear and bright.
Lu Qing sets the white-faced Cao Cao headdress on a wooden stand and combs the silk beard smooth with a bamboo comb.
Lu Qing rests against the mask-shell drying rack; tung-oil lamplight falls on his indigo short jacket.
Lu Qing opens the thread-bound face-pattern model book and checks it against the headdress formula.
He uses a vermilion brush to fill in painted-face brow lines and eye-socket finishes in the blank margins.
Lu Qing closes the model book and moves the white-faced Cao Cao headdress under a dust cover.
In the morning stage side chamber, Lu Qing greets young A-Tang dragging in the vermilion lacquer prop chest.

segments.action: Months later on a rainy night, Lu Qing keeps watch alone in the papier-mache atelier, the white-faced Cao Cao headdress on his knees.
Lu Qing opens the face-pattern model book; the cover is soaked through with tung oil, formulas blurred into a paste.

segments.action: The opera season stretches long; day after day Lu Qing mixes white powder, brushes base lacquer, and waits for hemp cores to dry in the shade.
Another snowy night, he tightens his indigo short jacket and trims tangled beards beside the tung-oil lamp.
At opening season, Lu Qing stands by the door tallying headdress loads carried out.
At high-summer noon he fans half-dry mask shells slowly with a fine fan.
Autumn rain falls on end; the atelier smells of tung oil, cinnabar, and damp xuan paper.
Another New Year's Eve, Lu Qing lines beards on wooden racks and keeps vigil alone in the atelier till dawn.
At dawn Lu Qing patrols along the stage side chamber; the vermilion lacquer prop chest leans by the mirror.
Lu Qing crouches to check whether the prop chest copper lock is fully bitten shut.
Lu Qing rearranges scattered greasepaint dishes by black, white, and vermilion.
An indigo-cloth prop box is carried into the side chamber—no twin-dragon relief, not the vermilion lacquer prop chest.
Fire breaks at midnight; thick smoke fills the papier-mache atelier, drying racks creaking in the heat.
In the glare of flame, the white face lacquer of the white-faced Cao Cao headdress cracks open, exposing the hemp cloth core.

segments.action: Half a copper lock from the vermilion lacquer prop chest hangs by the wall; Lu Qing wraps the still-blackened bolt in cloth.
He takes down one of the five tung-oil lamps from the beam and sits alone by its faint light.

After the new hemp core is pressed flat and powdered again, the white-faced Cao Cao headdress is usable once more, gold leaf slightly paler.

segments.action: A bamboo opera basket is carried into the stage side chamber packed with water sleeves—nothing to do with the burned vermilion lacquer prop chest.
Troupe master Old Xue enters the side chamber and talks beside Lu Qing; both wear indigo short jackets.
Old Xue points at the bamboo opera basket and asks for a separate water-sleeve rack; Lu Qing notes the size in the model-book margin.
From the next street comes Xiao Ju in a pale-pink apron; at a glance she somewhat resembles young A-Tang.
Xiao Ju tries to tidy a beard, but Lu Qing shakes his head—she wears a single braid; she is not A-Tang after all.
Years later at dusk, Lu Qing with his right arm wrapped in white cloth stands under the empty stage of the abandoned opera house.
